t.6.115.1: Having heard that supreme joy, Bharata, whose valour was true, the slayer of enemy heroes, gave orders to the delighted Śatrughna.
t.6.115.2: Let men who are pure worship all the deities and the sacred shrines of the city with fragrant garlands and with musical instruments.
t.6.115.3: Let the royal wives, and likewise the ministers, the soldiers, and the women of the army's companies go forth to behold Rāma's face, radiant like the moon.
t.6.115.4: Having heard Bharata's words, the valiant Śatrughna, slayer of enemy heroes, set many thousands of laborers to work.
t.6.115.5: Level the hollows and make the uneven places even, and from Nandigrāma onward let every obstructing spot be cleared away.
t.6.115.6: Let them sprinkle the whole earth with water cool as snow. Then others strewed parched grain and flowers everywhere.
t.6.115.7: Let the streets in this finest of cities have banners raised high, and let them adorn the houses by the time the sun rises.
t.6.115.8: Let men by the hundreds strew the royal highway, kept free of crowding, with garlands, wreaths and loose flowers, with fragrant perfumes and powders of five colors.
t.6.115.9: Some set out with thousands of rutting elephants adorned with gold, others with she-elephants bearing golden girths and accompanied by tuskers, and mighty chariot-warriors went forth in haste with their chariots.
t.6.115.10: Then all the wives of Daśaratha, having mounted their carriages and placing Kausalyā and Sumitrā at their head, set forth.
t.6.115.11: With the sound of the horses' hooves, the rumble of the chariot wheels, and the blare of conches and kettledrums, the earth seemed to tremble.
t.6.115.12: That entire city went to Nandigrāma, and so did the righteous-souled one, accompanied by the foremost of the twice-born and the chiefs of the guilds, together with the merchants.
t.6.115.13: Bharata was surrounded by ministers bearing garlands and sweets in their hands, and he was hailed by bards amid the sounding of conches and kettledrums.
t.6.115.14: The knower of dharma, bearing the noble one's feet upon his head, took up a white parasol adorned with white garlands.
t.6.115.15: Bearing also the two white yak-tail fans adorned with gold and fit for a king, he came, emaciated by fasting and wretched, clad in garments of bark and the skin of a black antelope.
t.6.115.16: Having heard of that arrival of his brother, the great-souled one, already filled with joy, then went forth together with his ministers to meet Rāma.
t.6.115.18: Then, when these words had been spoken thus, Hanūmān said this, making the matter known to Bharata, whose valour was true.
t.6.115.17: Looking around, Bharata spoke these words to the son of the Wind: "Surely the fickle-mindedness natural to monkeys is not being indulged here? For I do not see the noble Rāma Kākutstha, the scorcher of foes."
t.6.115.19: Having come upon trees that by the grace of Bharadvāja bore fruit in every season, were in full blossom, dripped with honey, and resounded with the humming of intoxicated bees,
t.6.115.20: And this boon was granted to him by Vāsava, O scorcher of foes, and then hospitality endowed with every excellence was offered to him together with his army.
t.6.115.21: A tremendous roar of the delighted forest-dwellers is heard; I think that army of monkeys is crossing the river Gomatī.
t.6.115.23: There, seen from afar, is that celestial aerial chariot Puṣpaka, spotless and shining like the moon, fashioned by Brahmā through the power of his mind.
t.6.115.22: Look at the shower of dust that has risen over towards the sandy river! I think the monkeys are shaking the lovely forest of sāla trees.
t.6.115.24: Having slain Rāvaṇa together with his kinsmen, the great-souled one has obtained, by the grace of Dhanada, this divine vehicle, swift as thought.
t.6.115.25: In this one are the two heroic brothers, the Rāghavas, together with Vaidehī, and also the greatly splendid Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas.
t.6.115.26: Then a shout born of joy rose and touched the heavens, proclaimed by women and children, young men and old: "This is Rāma!"
t.6.115.27: Having alighted from their chariots, elephants and horses, those men went down to the ground and beheld him standing in the aerial chariot, like the moon in the sky.
t.6.115.29: Seated in the aerial chariot created by Brahmā through his mind, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa, with his large and long eyes, shone like a second Vajrapāṇi.
t.6.115.28: Then Bharata, overjoyed, with joined palms and his face turned toward Rāghava, honored Rāma with a fitting welcome.
t.6.115.30: Then Bharata, bowing low, saluted his brother Rāma, who was seated at the front of the aerial chariot like the sun resting upon Mount Meru.
t.6.115.31: Made to ascend that aerial chariot, Bharata, whose valor was true, approached Rāma and, delighted, saluted him once again.
t.6.115.32: Raising him up, Kākutstha, filled with joy, took Bharata, who after a long time had come within the path of his eyes, onto his lap and embraced him.
t.6.115.33: Then Bharata, the scorcher of foes, approaching Lakṣmaṇa and Vaidehī, joyfully saluted them and spoke his own name.
t.6.115.34: The son of Kaikayī embraced Sugrīva, Jāmbavant and likewise Aṅgada, and Mainda, Dvivida, Nīla and Ṛṣabha as well.
t.6.115.35: Then those monkeys, able to take any form at will, assumed human shape and, overjoyed, asked Bharata about his welfare.
t.6.115.36: Bharata, speaking kindly to Vibhīṣaṇa, said these words: "By good fortune, with you as an ally, a most difficult deed has been accomplished."
t.6.115.37: Then Śatrughna too, having saluted Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, afterward humbly paid homage at Sītā's feet.
t.6.115.38: Rāma, approaching his mother, who was dejected and wasted with grief, bowed low and clasped her feet, gladdening his mother's heart.
t.6.115.39: Having saluted Sumitrā and the illustrious Kaikeyī, and then all the other mothers as well, he approached the family priest.
t.6.115.40: "Welcome to you, mighty-armed one, increaser of Kausalyā's joy!" Thus all the citizens, with palms joined in reverence, spoke to Rāma.
t.6.115.41: Bharata's elder brother beheld those thousands of joined palms held up by the citizens, like lotuses still in bud.
t.6.115.42: Bharata, the knower of dharma, himself took those sandals of Rāma and fitted them onto the feet of the lord of men.
t.6.115.43: Then Bharata, with joined palms, said to Rāma: "O king, this kingdom of yours, which I have guarded, is now returned to you by me."
t.6.115.44: Today my birth has attained its purpose and my heart's desire has been fulfilled, for I see you, the king, returned once more to Ayodhyā.
t.6.115.45: Let your honor inspect the treasury, the granary, the city and the army. By your splendor, I have made all of it tenfold.
t.6.115.46: Seeing Bharata, so devoted to his brother, speaking thus, the monkeys shed tears, and so did the rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.115.47: Then Rāghava, out of great joy, took Bharata onto his lap and, together with his army, went in that aerial chariot to Bharata's hermitage.
t.6.115.48: Then Rāghava, together with his army, having reached Bharata's hermitage, descended from the top of the aerial chariot and stood upon the surface of the earth.
t.6.115.49: And then Rāma said to that unsurpassed aerial chariot: "Carry the god Vaiśravaṇa; I give you leave, go now."
t.6.115.50: Then that unsurpassed aerial chariot, dismissed by Rāma, set out toward the northern quarter and went to the abode of Dhanada.
t.6.115.51: As Śakra, lord of the immortals, clasps the feet of Bṛhaspati, so Rāghava clasped the feet of the family priest, who was dear to him as his own self, and then the valiant one sat down together with him on a separate splendid seat.
